description.value: The Christina Lake Welcome Centre is a community hub opened in 2010 and located in the community park in the heart of Christina Lake, serving as both an interpretive centre and regional tourism information point. It houses a gallery of arts and crafts from Boundary region artists, a retail shop with locally produced items, and an innovative on-site Eco Machine wastewater treatment system that doubles as an environmental education exhibit. Per OSM tags, a coffee and dessert counter ('Lisa's coffee and desert') operates within the building, though this is not confirmed by the current website.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM description tag mentions 'Lisa's coffee and desert, BC Tourism information booth and Lake Stewardship information hub,' supporting the cafe categorisation, but the website content makes no mention of any cafe, coffee, or food service — it describes an arts gallery, retail shop, tourism information centre, and Eco Machine wastewater exhibit. Phone (250-447-6161) and address (1675 Highway 3) are confirmed by the website; OSM had no phone field. The absence of any food/drink confirmation on the website means all Food & Drink amenity criteria default to null.
concerns: Cafe/coffee component ('Lisa's coffee and desert') appears only in the OSM description tag — not mentioned anywhere on the website. May be a former sub-tenant or outdated information.
OSM had no phone number; 250-447-6161 was sourced from the website only.
Venue functions primarily as a tourism information centre and arts gallery (tourism=information tag), making 'Food & Drink' a potentially incorrect primary category.

Website references a separate site (http://www.christinalakearts.com) for the arts component — the OSM record and christinalake.ca URL appear to represent the destination/tourism organisation wrapper, not a standalone cafe business.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The cafe component driving the Food & Drink categorisation is evidenced only in OSM tags ('Lisa's coffee and desert') and is entirely absent from the website, which presents this venue as a tourism information/arts centre. A human reviewer should confirm whether food/drink service is still active before listing under Food & Drink; if confirmed, it would be a useful cyclist waypoint on Highway 3 with tourism info and regional maps.
enrichment_extras.notes: The website is the official Christina Lake destination marketing site (christinalake.ca), and the Welcome Centre page is one section of it. The tourism@christinalake.ca email address is confirmed on both the main Welcome Centre page and the Contact Us subpage.
